name: pptx
description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions \"deck,\" \"slides,\" \"presentation,\" or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.

name: sdu-sprint-odt-report
description: Generates plain-language, step-by-step ODT walkthrough reports for SDU Help Desk Bot sprints (e.g. "create the Sprint 3 ODT", "make a step-by-step report for this sprint", "I need the walkthrough document with screenshot instructions"). Use this skill whenever the user asks for a sprint implementation report in ODT format that explains spreadsheet user-story cells in plain language, shows how each requirement was implemented on the Buda platform, explains how to demonstrate it to a teacher, and tells the reader exactly what to screenshot. Trigger this even if the user just says "make the walkthrough doc" or "give me the ODT for this sprint" without repeating the full format description — they mean this exact format, established in a prior sprint.

name: sdu-sprint-xlsx-stories
description: Generates copy-paste-ready xlsx user-story and QA sheets for future SDU Help Desk Bot sprints (e.g. "generate the xlsx for US-05", "make the user story and QA sheet for the next sprint", "I need a spreadsheet tab I can paste into the project sheet"). Use this skill whenever the user asks for a new user story + QA test sheet in the exact format already used by US-01/US-01-QA and US-02/US-02-QA in the project spreadsheet. Trigger even if they just say "make the next sprint's story sheet" without repeating the full format — they mean this exact layout.

name: sdu-workspace-backup
description: Creates a complete, portable .tar.gz backup of the SDU Help Desk workspace — including all agent config/persona files (SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, USER.md, IDENTITY.md, MEMORY.md, TOOLS.md, HEARTBEAT.md), memory notes, custom skills (.agents/skills/), .buda/works build scripts, and the full sdu-helpdesk-bot project (knowledge_base, documents, query_log, session_logs, tests, writeup). Trigger whenever the user says "backup", "make a backup", "export the workspace", or asks to save a snapshot of the project and settings.

name: web-app-builder
description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to build, scaffold, modify, debug, or ship a web application, including React/Vite/Next.js/Vue/Svelte apps, full-stack prototypes, dashboards, landing pages with interactivity, games, admin panels, CRUD apps, API-backed UIs, authentication flows, database-connected apps, or when they say things like \"build a web app\", \"make a frontend\", \"create a SaaS prototype\", \"turn this idea into an app\", \"搭建 Web 应用\", \"做一个网站应用\", or \"帮我开发前端\". This skill should trigger even if the user does not explicitly mention a framework, because it guides framework selection, project structure, implementation, testing, live preview, and Git commits after each working slice.

name: buda-automations
description: Use this skill when the user wants to schedule, list, or delete recurring agent tasks in Buda. Trigger on explicit requests (\"create a daily automation\", \"set up a cron job\", \"show my scheduled tasks\", \"delete this automation\") and indirect signals (\"every morning\", \"once a day\", \"remind me weekly\", \"check every hour\", \"run this automatically\"). Also trigger when the user describes a repeated or timed action without using the word \"automation\".

name: far
description: File-Augmented Retrieval — generate persistent .meta sidecar files for PDFs, images, spreadsheets, videos and more, making every binary file readable to AI coding agents.

name: buda-machine-info
description: Use this skill when the user asks about their Buda sandbox environment: CPU, memory, disk, OS, kernel, or installed software versions. Trigger on direct questions (\"how much RAM?\", \"what OS?\", \"check disk space\") and indirect ones (\"can this run Docker?\", \"am I out of memory?\", \"what tools are available?\"). Also use when troubleshooting resource constraints or deciding whether the sandbox can handle a workload, even without keywords like \"system info\" or \"specs\".

name: buda-web-preview
description: Use this skill when the user wants to create, view, run, or preview any web page, HTML file, game, landing page, demo, prototype, or frontend project.

name: find-skills
description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

name: skill-creator
description: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, update or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
